text:
RETAIL CONDUCT AUTHORITY FICTIONAL REGULATOR - SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE
Final rule: Customers in vulnerable circumstances
Notice number: RCN-2026-010
Issued by: Retail Conduct Authority
Published: 2026-10-06
Effective date: 2027-02-01
1. Who this applies to
All firms that serve retail customers.
2. Background
Health problems, life events, low financial resilience or low capability can make customers more likely to suffer harm. Firms should notice and respond.
3. Requirements
3.1 A firm must record, with the customer's consent, any vulnerability a customer discloses, so that staff can adapt how they serve that customer.
3.2 A firm must train customer-facing staff to recognize and respond to signs of vulnerability at least once a year.
4. Status
Firms must comply with the requirements in section 3 from 2027-02-01.

obligations.text: A firm must record, with the customer's consent, any vulnerability a customer discloses, so that staff can adapt how they serve that customer.
obligations.controlDesc: Annual vulnerability training completion report for customer-facing colleagues
obligations.reason: Policy POL-VUL-01 states "With the customer's consent, colleagues record disclosed vulnerabilities in the customer profile so service can be adapted," which exactly matches the obligation's requirement to record disclosed vulnerabilities with consent for service adaptation, and Control CTL-181 monitors this through quarterly review of vulnerability flags recorded with consent.

obligations.text: A firm must train customer-facing staff to recognize and respond to signs of vulnerability at least once a year.
obligations.controlDesc: Annual vulnerability training completion report for customer-facing colleagues
obligations.reason: Policy POL-VUL-01 states "All customer-facing colleagues complete vulnerability training every year" which matches the obligation's requirement for training at least once a year, and Control CTL-182 monitors this through an "Annual vulnerability training completion report for customer-facing colleagues."
